title: Big Data Analytics for Governed Human–AI Invention: A Neuro-Symbolic Framework for Business Model Innovation Screening
content: Big data analytics can reveal technical and market opportunities, but business model innovation also requires organizations to generate, evaluate, and govern conjectures about how value will be created, delivered, and captured. Large language models enlarge this search space while sometimes producing unsupported or inconsistent explanations. We present a neuro-symbolic analytics framework combining claim-level epistemic labeling, abductive logic programming, counter-abduction, evidence retrieval, versioned constraints, provenance, and accountable human decisions. Each candidate is represented as a traceable object linking its technical mechanism to proposed changes in value proposition, value creation, value delivery, and value capture. Among 642 shared-response questions containing an adjudicated hallucination, screened invention-candidate yield was 0.46 for the full framework versus 0.25 for structured ideation, a configuration-level difference of 21.0 percentage points (95% question-cluster CI: 17.4–24.6; p&lt;0.001). Unsafe promotion was 11.0 percentage points lower (95% CI: 7.8–14.2), and reviewer effort was 2.3 min per question lower (95% CI: 1.5–3.1). These comparisons do not identify the causal contribution of individual modules. A fixed-bed reactor case illustrates how an unsupported mechanism can be converted into a bounded conceptual alternative without being represented as validated engineering knowledge. Hall2Invent is an intentionally challenging benchmark rather than a representative sample of professional work, and no human-only, operational, or longitudinal business outcomes were observed. The paper therefore demonstrates technical candidate screening within the benchmark; transportability, realized business-model change, and firm performance remain prospective validation targets.
